Ken Paxton

Republican candidate for U.S. Senator, Texas · Open seat

Texas Attorney General

Attorney general since 2015 after 10 years in the Texas House and two in the Texas Senate. Won the May 26 Republican runoff over Sen. John Cornyn with 63.8% after President Trump endorsed him. He was impeached by the Texas House in 2023 and acquitted on all charges by the Texas Senate. Did not answer the Texas Tribune questionnaire, so positions below come from his past public statements.

Where Paxton stands

Gas tax
Supports permanently repealing the federal gas tax and keeping oil and gas regulation low to raise production.
Data centers
Supports efficient water use, having the industry pay its own infrastructure costs, ending state sales tax breaks, and keeping facilities away from homes.
Iran and war powers
Backs the president's actions on Iran; says he will decide on funding after getting more intelligence.
Border wall in Big Bend
Called the plans "not smart border security" and welcomed the August pause.
Gender care for minors
Opposes it; as attorney general he extended the state ban to mental health providers.
Marijuana and hemp
Has sued Dallas over marijuana decriminalization; no direct comment found on Texas THC rules.
